---
title: "WF4 — Simulate system"
---

`simulate_system.smk` runs Wflow-SBM for explicit series in a ready WF3 collection and reduces retained native responses to named indicator sets. Invoke it through `scripts/simulate_system.py`, which validates the selected operations and indicator sets before Snakemake starts.

## Rules

| Rule | Operation |
|---|---|
| `all` (target) | Collect the selected indicator set and records. |
| 4.01 `write_model_fingerprint` | Record the model reference. |
| 4.02 `check_model_unchanged` | Verify the live model against its reference. |
| 4.03 `snapshot_simulation_inputs` | Freeze collection, model, settings, and environment identity. |
| 4.04 `downscale_scenario_series` | Prepare per-run model forcing. |
| 4.05 `run_wflow_simulations_batch_<batch>` | Run Wflow in batches, retaining native responses. |
| 4.06 `publish_wflow_outputs` | Publish the response inventory. |
| `simulations_only` (target) | Collect simulation outputs without indicators. |
| 4.07 `prepare_indicator_plan` | Resolve each distinct indicator request's identity and targets. |
| 4.08 `derive_system_indicators` | Produce each immutable indicator set: tables, coverage evidence and marker. |
| 4.09 `gather_logs` | Merge experiment logs. |
| 4.10 `gather_benchmarks` | Merge experiment benchmarks. |
| `simulations_and_indicators` (target) | Collect the selected indicator set. |

The runner infers its target from `operations`: both operations run `all`, simulations alone stop at `simulations_only`, and indicators alone read completed responses without rerunning Wflow. Sets with identical numerical requests share one plan and one immutable indicator set. After Snakemake, the runner publishes each set separately; a failed set keeps its previous publication, and the command exits nonzero unless every set is current. With several sets, Snakemake runs with `--keep-going`, which also lets independent Wflow batches continue after one fails.

## Rule flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["4.01–4.03 Verify model and freeze inputs"] --> B["4.04 Downscale series"]
  B --> C["4.05 Run Wflow batches"]
  C --> D["4.06 Publish responses"]
  D --> E["4.07 Plan indicators"]
  E --> F["4.08 Derive indicator set"]
  D --> G["simulations_only target"]
  F --> H["simulations_and_indicators target"]
  D --> I["4.09–4.10 Records"]
  F --> I
```

Indicators alone start from existing retained responses and proceed through the indicator branch. Simulations alone stop after response publication.

## Configuration

The project file supplies the `model` context and `workflows.simulate_system.enabled` and `.config_path`; the latter resolves the workflow YAML beside the project file. The WF4 file, `test_case/project_config_rapid_simulate_system.yml`, sets `experiment_name` (the output namespace), `operations` and `indicator_sets`. The template at `config/templates/example-basin/project_config_simulate_system.yml` also describes the optional `compute` block: `julia_threads`, `max_parallel_batches`, `batch_size_max`, `batch_size`, and `disk_headroom_gb`.

```yaml
experiment_name: experiment_rapid
operations: [simulations, indicators]   # either alone; omitted means both
indicator_sets: [default, example_subset]
indicator_set_definitions:
  example_subset:
    config_path: indicator_sets/example_subset.yml   # relative to this file
```

`operations` is a nonempty list of unique entries from `simulations` and `indicators`; order does not matter.
`indicator_sets` lists set ids (`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, at most 64 characters); omitted means `[default]`.
`default` is bundled at `config/indicator_sets/default.yml` and expands to the existing suite for
`model.outvars` (the toolbox defaults when the key is absent, or the retained variables when indicators
run alone). A custom set's `config_path` may be absolute; a relative path resolves against the WF4 file
that declares it. Selected set files are read once per invocation. Copy
`config/templates/indicator_set.template.yml` for a custom set: it selects registered definitions,
or names one registered calculation under an authored id. A set never defines arithmetic, units,
calendars, missingness or grain.

To add environmental-flow indicators, use `indicator_sets: [default, eflow-erfa]`, or select
`[eflow-erfa]` alone. This set requires retained daily discharge (`q`) and supplies 70 indicators:
the median and interquartile range of each of 35 annual metrics, grouped into high flow, monthly flow,
low flow, rates/frequencies of change, and intermittency. Names follow `q_<metric>_<med|iqr>`.
It ports the default conventions of `eflowrisk`'s daily-flow extension of IHA/ERFA; it does not produce
ecological risk classes or baseline/scenario comparisons.

The configured water year applies. Years need at least 90% finite daily observations and monthly
means need 80% of their calendar month's days; incomplete edge years can therefore be excluded.
Pulse thresholds are the individual record's 90th/10th percentiles, with strict exceedances; zero
sequences include discharge at or below zero. Rolling windows and daily differences cross year
boundaries, while pulse runs split there. Timing uses the first occurrence and linear day-of-water-year
statistics. Group results average member indicators with equal weights, propagating undefined values.
See the [set conventions](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/blueearth_cst/indicators/sets/eflow_erfa/README.md)
for all fixed defaults and interpretation limits.

The `crop-water` set supplies ten seasonal or annual agricultural screening indicators from discharge,
precipitation, PET, AET and net recharge. It requires daily retained responses for all five variables.
Use `model.outvars` to retain them in a new simulation; existing experiments without PET must be
regenerated under a fresh experiment name. The summer low-flow declaration also needs one fixed,
location-keyed historical Qcrit with source and baseline provenance. Copy the bundled
`config/indicator_sets/crop-water.yml` to a case file with the same `id`, replace `selection.registry`
with a mapping that supplies `overrides.summer_low_flow_days`, and bind that file using
`indicator_set_definitions.crop-water.config_path`. An explicit custom definition may replace this
bundled selector; the `default` preset cannot be replaced. The
[set conventions](../../../blueearth_cst/indicators/sets/crop_water/README.md) define periods,
formulas, the Qcrit record, diagnostics and interpretation limits. The ET ratios use Wflow landscape
AET and reference PET as screening proxies; subcatchment means do not represent crop or aquifer areas.

Selected indicators must be available: before simulating, all their required variables are checked
against `model.outvars`; when indicators run alone, against the retained responses. A missing variable
fails with the set, indicator, method and variable; it never schedules a simulation.

The scalar `operation: simulate-and-indicators | indicators-only` and `indicators:` token list remain accepted for one feature release as the legacy interface, with their explicit `--target` rules. They cannot be mixed with `operations`/`indicator_sets`; see `dev/records/milestones/post-r12/migration_named-indicator-sets.md`.

## Inputs

WF4 can run with WF3 disabled when its selected collection is already ready. For a project-generation
selection, the runner binds any pending experiment seed from the validated existing generation plan
together with the collection. It preserves an already-bound seed and does not regenerate scenarios.

WF4 requires the completed WF1 model and an explicitly selected ready WF3 collection and run IDs. It checks the model reference and freezes the selected collection, model, settings, and environment identity for the experiment. It does not consume WF2 projections.

## Outputs

An experiment retains native Wflow response CSVs and a response inventory. New immutable indicator sets use
`indicator-set/5`, under `_engine/indicator_sets/<id>/`. They retain `indicators.json`, indicator tables, group
membership, declarations, return-level evidence, per-series block coverage and the execution context.
Each selected set has a readable view at `results/indicator_sets/<set-id>/`: run and group tables, group
lookups and an `indicators.csv` dictionary. See [Reading the outputs](../guide/outputs.md).

## Local calculation sets

`blueearth_cst/indicators/` provides a plain Python interface independent of WF4 files and Snakemake.
Its [authoring guide](../../../blueearth_cst/indicators/README.md) documents contracts, dependencies,
parameters, independent checks and extension examples. Trusted installed sets own formulas in
`calculations.py`, registrations and fixed `ASSUMPTIONS` in `registry.py`, independent numerical
checks in `checks.py`, and local guidance in `README.md`. Assumptions describe implemented choices;
they do not offer alternative scientific methods. The water-year anchor remains explicit context.

The optional bundled `flow_regime` set includes the matched prototype aliases and whole-period mean,
plus five rolling extremes and daily change indicators. Its recharge entry requires retained `gwr`.
`flood_risk` declares 2, 5, 10, 15 and 20-year discharge hazard levels. It remains opt-in, and the
production probability qualification gate permits only 2 and 10 years with the shipped evidence.
Selecting the entire example therefore fails explicitly at an unsupported probability. Select an
eligible local calculation explicitly for a confined qualified calculation:

```yaml
schema_version: 1
id: flood_10
title: Ten-year discharge hazard
description: Annual maximum discharge; no exposure or damage calculation.
selection:
  indicators:
    - id: peak_10
      title: Ten-year annual maximum discharge
      description: Qualified production GEV estimator and screening requirements.
      references: []
      calculation:
        set: flood_risk
        method: flood_return_level/1
        parameters: {return_period: 10}
```

`selection: {registry: flow_regime}` selects all registrations of that trusted module. An authored
entry's optional `calculation.set` selects a trusted local callable. YAML cannot import a file path or
execute Python. Legacy definitions and authored aliases retain their existing spelling and behavior.
New local calculations have explicit set/indicator identities and need no `equivalent_definition`.

## Integrity and numerical rechecking

Discover indicator sets on demand with:

```powershell
pixi run python scripts/inspect_indicators.py --experiment <experiment-root> --list
pixi run python scripts/inspect_indicators.py --experiment <experiment-root> --manifest <indicators.json>
pixi run python scripts/inspect_indicators.py --experiment <experiment-root> --manifest <indicators.json> --recheck
```

The default command checks saved hashes, completion identity and artifact structure. It imports no
current calculation registry and needs no original discharge input. It reports matching saved check
receipts as **historical** evidence. Hash consistency does not prove authenticity against coordinated
edits of artifacts and manifests.

`--recheck` additionally requires matching execution sources, definitions, original input identity and
recorded dependencies. It invokes current independent set checkers and records their hashes and current
runtime in a new receipt. Changed checker-only code is allowed; it receives fresh attribution. A missing
or changed input blocks numerical rechecking while preserving artifact inspection. A requested recheck
exits nonzero if unavailable or unsuccessful. Both scripts support `--traceback` for diagnosis.

The strict production reader retains its input and cache validity checks. Integrity inspection never
makes a stale result reusable. Existing `/3` and `/4` publications remain readable without rewriting;
their missing execution context conservatively prevents fresh numerical eligibility. See the
[migration note](../../../dev/records/milestones/post-r12/migration-structured-metrics.md).
